$schema_note: Machine-readable companion to bonsai2-floor.md, for the installer. Every number carries a provenance tag: MEASURED (this machine, date given), PUBLISHED (source URL), API (read from the public Hugging Face or GitHub API on the date given), ESTIMATE (arithmetic on tagged inputs, formula in `estimate_method`), UNMEASURED (no evidence; the installer must benchmark on the device before it promises a speed). Sections: model_family (every size and packing, with a download manifest), runtime (the fork, per-backend release assets, the runtime check), reserves, detection (what to read and how), pick (the ordered decision procedure), tiers (the expected outcome per hardware class, with the headroom arithmetic shown), floor.
supersedes: version 1 of the same day: adds the manifest with sha256, the per-backend release assets, the structured pick, the detection commands, and corrects the 6 GB and 8 GB Windows GPU tiers to partial offload (the 2,560 MiB display reserve leaves less than the 5,672 MiB of weights).

model_family.publisher: PrismML (prism-ml on Hugging Face; PrismML-Eng on GitHub)
model_family.license_all: Apache-2.0 (API 2026-09-30 for every repo listed; also in the GGUF headers of the 4B and the mmproj, MEASURED)

bonsai2.one_size_note: Bonsai 2 ships at ONE size. Base: Qwen3.8-27B (GGUF arch `qwen35`: 64 blocks, gated-DeltaNet linear attention with full attention every 4th block, 4 KV heads x 256, 262,144 training context). Every smaller Bonsai file is the earlier Bonsai (1-bit) or Ternary Bonsai (1.58-bit) generation on Qwen3 bases.

kv_cache.note: 16 full-attention layers x 4 KV heads x 256 dims x 2 (K,V) x 2 bytes = 64 KiB/token at f16. PUBLISHED (atomic.chat) and consistent with the MEASURED header. The DeltaNet layers hold a small fixed recurrent state per slot, not per token.

runtime.required: PrismML fork of llama.cpp, branch `prism`; stock llama.cpp REFUSES ggml types 142/143 (issue https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29058, open 2026-09-30); Ollama and LM Studio cannot load them; a `Q2_0` file on a stock build loads silently and outputs gibberish (no Hadamard activation transform).

release_assets.note: Asset name pattern `llama-{tag}-bin-{platform}.{zip|tar.gz}` from the GitHub release. The installer downloads exactly one runtime asset for the detected (os, backend); CUDA builds on Windows also need the matching `cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-{ver}-x64.zip` unless the driver already ships the runtime. All sizes MiB, API 2026-09-30.

steps: `llama-server --version` prints `build NNNNN` with NNNNN >= 10658 and the binary is the fork asset just installed (stock builds print a different version string and will refuse the file later)

`llama-bench --list-devices` lists the device the pick expects (CUDA0 / Metal / Vulkan0 / ROCm0); a GPU tier whose build sees no device is re-planned as the CPU tier of the same RAM, and the user is told which driver is missing
a 1,000-token `llama-bench -p 128 -n 32` on the downloaded file must produce a row; a refusal names the tensor type and means the wrong runtime, not a bad file (the sha256 already matched)

gpu: -np 2 --kv-unified (T5+) so background probes do not queue behind a chat turn
-b 4096 -ub 2048 on T5+ (prompt 370 -> 467 tok/s on a 16K prompt, MEASURED 2026-09-18); -b 2048 -ub 512 on T4/T4a
--mmproj <mmproj> on T5+; on T4/T4a only when the user turns vision on

friday_footprint_mib.provenance: ESTIMATE (server + tray + one browser tab); the installer measures its own RSS after boot and writes the real number

compute_buffer_mib.provenance: ESTIMATE from llama.cpp allocation logs of comparable models; the bench replaces it

estimate_method.decode_tok_s_cpu: 0.7 * memory_bandwidth_gb_s / 5.5  (bandwidth-bound; 5.5 GB = PTQ1_0 weight traffic per token excluding the embedding row; 0.7 = fraction the community AVX2 kernels reached on single-channel DDR5, PUBLISHED issue #196)
estimate_method.decode_tok_s_partial_offload: 1 / (f_gpu / gpu_tok_s + f_cpu / cpu_tok_s)  where f_gpu is the fraction of weight bytes on the GPU (the layers offloaded), gpu_tok_s the tier's full-offload figure and cpu_tok_s the CPU estimate for the host's RAM
estimate_method.decode_tok_s_gpu: interpolated by memory bandwidth between PUBLISHED L4 32.1, RTX 4090 91.1, RTX 5090 120.5 (PTQ1_0) and MEASURED RTX 4070 30-36
estimate_method.prompt_tok_s: CPU: ~2x decode (PUBLISHED 16 vs 8.3). GPU: PUBLISHED PP512 figures; 467 MEASURED here on a 16K prompt
estimate_method.seat_mib: weights_mib + context * kib_per_token / 1024 + compute_buffer_mib + (600 if mmproj loaded)
estimate_method.n_gpu_layers: floor(64 * (usable_vram - kv_mib - compute_mib) / weights_mib), clamped to [0, 64]; if >= 64 then 99 (full offload); if < 24 then 0 (CPU tier: fewer than a third of the layers on the GPU is not worth the transfer)

detection.purpose: What the preflight reads, how, and which pick input each feeds. Everything is local; nothing is sent (amendment A3).

fields.field: cpu.flags: avx2, avx512, avx_vnni, amx, neon
fields.how: Windows/Linux: cpuid leaf 7 via a ctypes probe (or /proc/cpuinfo flags on Linux); macOS: sysctl machdep.cpu.features / arm64 implies NEON
fields.feeds: floor (AVX2 required on x86), kernel path

fields.how: SMBIOS module type, speed, channel count (Windows); `unified` on Apple Silicon; Linux: dmidecode if root else unknown
fields.feeds: CPU tier speed estimate (T1 vs T2)

fields.field: gpus[]: vendor, name, vram_total_mib, vram_used_mib, driver, compute_class
fields.how: NVIDIA: nvidia-smi (in tree). AMD: rocm-smi / Win32_VideoController AdapterRAM. Intel/other: vulkaninfo --summary deviceName + heap sizes; Win32_VideoController. Apple: system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType (unified)
fields.exists_in_tree: NVIDIA only (hardware_profile.detect_gpus); others are floor build item 1

fields.how: MIN_DISPLAY_RESERVE_MIB by OS, reconciled with the live counter with impossible values rejected
shutil.disk_usage on the Friday home; optional 256 MiB read-rate sample

pick.purpose: The ordered decision the installer runs. First matching rule wins. Every rule's output is then dry-run through residency_policy.plan(); a refusal (R1 os-reserve, R2 ram-ceiling, R3 vram-budget, R8 disk-headroom) is shown with its numbers and the next rule down is tried.
pick.packing_rule: PQ2_0 when the device is NVIDIA Ampere/Hopper/Blackwell (compute_class consumer-bf16, datacenter-fp8, or name contains 'rtx 50'), AMD RDNA (hip), or Apple M5 AND usable memory holds it at the tier's context; otherwise PTQ1_0. CPU tiers: always PTQ1_0.

rules.note: the reference machine: 12,282 - 2,560 = 9,722 usable; seat 5,671 + 1,536 KV + 1,200 compute + 600 mmproj = 9,007; 715 spare. 64K measured with 495 MiB spare beside a loaded desktop; 49K is the shipped value.
8 GB cards on LINUX (8,192 - 512 = 7,680 usable): seat 5,671 + 512 + 400 = 6,583. On WINDOWS an 8 GB card has 8,192 - 2,560 = 5,632 usable, below the weights, so it falls to T4a.

PARTIAL OFFLOAD. Windows 8 GB: 5,632 usable - 256 KV - 400 compute = 4,976 for weights -> 56 of 64 layers. Windows 6 GB: 3,584 - 656 = 2,928 -> 33 layers. Linux 6 GB: 5,632 -> 56 layers. The rest of the weights live in RAM, so the RAM floor (T1) applies too. Speed by estimate_method.decode_tok_s_partial_offload.
THE FLOOR. Windows: 16,384 - 6,144 - 1,500 = 8,740 budget; seat 5,671 + 512 + 400 = 6,583; 2,157 spare for the browser. 16K also fits (7,095) and is allowed when the user asks.

Refuse with the numbers (bonsai2-floor.md §6.2); offer the cloud path (A6); if decision D1 is yes, offer Ternary Bonsai 4B PQ2_0 (1,025 MiB; needs ram_budget >= 2,500) or 1.7B (442 MiB), labelled as the older, weaker generation.

profiles.gpu: full tool registry (min_tool_context), thinking at medium, streaming, 2 slots where listed
profiles.cpu: tool_selector top-12 (~1,700 tokens) instead of the ~8,600-token registry; thinking off for the core loop; one slot; --cache-reuse 256; the once-per-session prefix cost stated to the user in seconds
profiles.below-floor: no local brain seat; cloud path or D1

pick.disk_rule: download allowed only if disk.free_mib - sum(manifest bytes to fetch) >= 10240 (R8); the runtime asset (12-560 MiB) counts too

floor.name: APPLICATION FLOOR (Friday's published minimum)
floor.statement: 16 GB of RAM; x86-64 with AVX2 and at least 4 physical cores (6 recommended), or Apple Silicon with 16 GB; Windows 10/11 64-bit, macOS 14+, or Linux x86-64/arm64; 20 GB free disk; a one-time 6.6 GB download. Any discrete GPU with 6 GB or more of memory lifts the machine into a GPU tier (partial offload at 6-8 GB on Windows); it does not replace the RAM requirement.
floor.why_16gb: Windows: 6,144 OS reserve + 1,500 Friday + 5,671 weights + 512 KV (8K) + 400 compute = 14,227 of 16,384 MiB. 8 GB machines cannot hold the weights beside the OS. 12 GB machines page as soon as a browser opens.
floor.core_loop_test: after the session's first turn, one spoken or typed turn that calls one tool and answers finishes in under 60 s; decode >= 3 tok/s; conformance gate >= 8/10. A machine that fails is told the numbers and offered the cloud path; its tier record is corrected.
floor.prompt_cost: full registry ~8.6K tokens at ~16 tok/s = ~9 min cold; CPU profile ~1.7K tokens = ~2 min once per session, seconds per turn after (prompt cache).

cpu_only_2026-09-30.machine: i7-10700F 8c/16t AVX2, 32 GB DDR4 (42.7 GB/s SMBIOS estimate), GPU hidden with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="", fork build 10685
cpu_only_2026-09-30.conditions: PROVISIONAL: the PC was busy with other sessions' builds. No SUITE_LOCK was held. Free RAM and CPU load were sampled every 5 s by the driver script.

runs.status: PROVISIONAL (loaded machine; generic CPU kernel because --no-repack was needed for PQ2_0 on CPU)

NOT OBTAINED: killed at the 1,500 s cap with no result row; the weights paged (peak RSS 3,680 of 5,671 MiB; RAM available fell from 4,357 to 251 MiB; CPU 86.9% average during). A paged number is not a number.
NOT RUN: stopped before start because the 8-thread run had already shown the weights do not fit in the free RAM, and holding 251 MiB free was starving the other sessions.

cpu_only_2026-09-30.what_it_means: The 27B on CPU needs the 5.7 GB of weights resident; with under 6 GB of RAM actually free it pages and the installer must treat that as T0-for-now, not as a slow T1. The floor's 16 GB line assumes the OS reserve (6,144) and Friday (1,500) are the only other tenants. A quiet-machine rerun is still owed; the installer's own bench at install time is the number that ships.

first_setup_rule: ONLY Bonsai 2 27B is suggested at first setup, at the packing, context and offload the pick returns. Gemma, Qwen and every other local family remain fully supported by explicit choice and are never refused (the seat gate is a no-op by maintainer decision).
knock_on: FridayWeaver-2 trains on Bonsai 2 (Friday-Models; decision D3). The Gemma E2B lineage stops at FridayWeaver-1.
